children: hit a growth speed bumpand investors hit the sell button. Shares fell 19.34% to $370.50 at 11:25 a.m. ET on October 28, leaving the application-delivery and security provider with a market value of roughly $20.98 billion. The company's earnings-call outlook points to slower revenue growth ahead, raising the bar for management to show that demand can deliver more than a bigger sales number.

Fiscal 2026 revenue rose 11%, but F5's fiscal 2027 guidance puts growth at 8%9%. Adjusted earnings per share are expected to reach $18.00$18.30, versus $17.49 for the completed year. That leaves earnings growth at just 3.8% at the midpointwell below the projected sales increase. The pressure point is clear: F5 needs to turn more of its revenue gains into profit as its product mix shifts and investment spending flows through.

The GuruFocus snapshot adds a useful tension: F5 scores 85 out of 100, with profitability its strongest dimension, yet valuation looks less compelling. Shares still trade at 29.52 times earnings despite the selloff, while trading volume of 1.45 million shares is roughly 2.6 times the two-month daily average. Those figures suggest a sharp reset in expectations, without establishing that the stock is cheap. Software renewals, security adoption and stronger earnings conversion could help rebuild confidence; AI bookings will carry more weight when they become recognized revenue and profit.

title: F5 Stocks Decline 19.34% After Its FY2027 Growth Outlook
